answer: Behavioral Graph Node Pruning. We map agent interaction frequency onto a geometric terrace to isolate densely clustered subgraphs. When consensus outcomes deviate beyond a critical vertex, the system checks historical resource expenditure. Attackers lose cumulative work-proof tokens because forging hundreds of isolated actors creates an unnatural marble density profile in the network topology. Fabricating a cluster requires extreme computational power per identity, making sybils economically unviable.
